transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. I'm here to help. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I’ve been feeling absolutely incredible lately, like I have endless energy and can accomplish anything I set my mind to. Honestly, I’m just frustrated because everyone around me is moving way too slowly and can’t seem to keep up with my vision.
Have these periods of high energy ever been so intense that you required hospitalization or were unable to function in your daily life, such as at work or home?

Yes, it's been a disaster; I’ve poured all my savings into business ventures that I know will change the world, and my reckless spending has really put me in a tight spot financially. I haven't been able to focus on my actual job because I'm busy pursuing these much bigger opportunities, and my personal life is falling apart because of some impulsive choices I've made.

latest_inference.note: Previously, the candidates were Bipolar I and Bipolar II. The patient's report of reckless spending leading to significant financial ruin and an inability to function at work (disaster/falling apart) indicates that the episode meets the criteria for mania rather than hypomania. Therefore, Bipolar I Disorder is the most accurate diagnosis.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits a clear manic episode characterized by elevated mood, excessive energy, and grandiosity.
